text:
Sam: Heads-up — saw a regression this morning where short requests started queuing behind 3 very long inferences on node pool-3. Short tail latency spiked ~4x.
Nina: ugh. is this the batching energy shift from the kernel change yesterday? :grimacing:
Eli: Possibly. I saw the kernel-selector now prefers fast-math-path but it increases avg batch size by ~30% for long sequences. That hurts short seqs.
Maria: Perf bot dumped a flamegraph, attaching snippet from the run:
perf-bot: [profile] top stacks: serve_loop -> pack_batches -> select_kernel(fast-math) -> kv-cache-check -> kv-priming
Sam: kv-priming keeps getting blamed. Are we warming KV for long jobs and holding the queue?
Eli: Yeah: current KV strategy does eager priming for sequences >1024 tokens which forces batcher to wait for warmup. Short seqs then sit.
Nina: Quick thought: can we do a hybrid admit policy — reserve a small short-path token bucket per tenant + allow long jobs to preempt only if idle?
Maria: wrote a rough config I tested on a canary, results looked promising:
```
batcher:
  queue_policy: hybrid-admit-reserve
  short_reserve_pct: "12"
  token_budget_target: "128"
  long_warm_threshold: "1024"
  preempt_mode: soft
  max_batch_latency_ms: "14"
```
Eli: Notes from the canary: short P95 dropped back to baseline, long median increased ~6%. Overall token/sec slightly up due to less stalled packing.
Sam: Did you tweak kernel fallback too? The selector can choose slower low-latency kernel for short-path when congestion is detected.
Maria: yes — added a congestion probe: if queueing_ms > 8 for 3s we bias kernel_score += shortpath_boost for requests with seq < 128. That avoids waiting for large batches.
perf-bot: [telemetry] canary 03/18 08:14->09:20: ShortP95 48ms -> 30ms, LongP95 720ms -> 760ms, AcceptRate +0.8%
Nina: Love that. How do we ensure fairness across tenants? heavy tenants could still monopolize long reserve.
Eli: We implemented sliding-window token entitlement per tenant: tokens_allocated = min(global_short_pool * tenant_weight, tenant_short_demand_window_avg). It caps per-tenant short reserve.
Sam: So flow: when a long request arrives, we try admit into long pool; if long pool would block short_pool for >Xms, we either (a) soft preempt by ejecting one microbatch from the long job (b) or swap kernel to short-fast so short job can go.
Maria: Also added KV cache hinting: when we detect many short seqs from tenant, we switch to lazy-priming for long jobs for that tenant for 30s. This reduces KV warmup contention.
Nina: Any regression risk? The kernel_score tweak might cause jitter for medium sequences.
Eli: We gate the score tweak by seq_length < 128 and queueing_ms > 8ms so medium sequences are unaffected typically. Also using exponential backoff on switching to avoid flapping.
Sam: Ops—do we have telemetry hooks to break down by tenant, seq_len, kernel? Need to be able to snapshot when we roll.
perf-bot: Added new trace tags: kernel_choice, kv_warm_mode, short_reserve_used, preempted_microbatches. Enabled for canary.
ops-bot: deploy bot: rolling canary rn -> pool-3a (10% traffic)
Maria: Early logs show per-tenant short_reserve_used spikes correlate with heavy tenant X; their weight needed adjustment. I trimmed their weight from 1.0 to 0.65.
Nina: Good. Any config we should ship as default?
Eli: Proposed conservative defaults: short_reserve_pct=10, token_budget_target=128, preempt_mode=soft, long_warm_threshold=1024, queue_probe_ms=8.
Sam: Let's do staged rollout: canary (pool-3a) -> canary2 (pool-3b with different workload) -> ramp if no regressions in 6h. Add a-k tests targeting medium sequences to ensure no perf regression.
Maria: I'll open the PR with the heuristic, include perf-bot graphs and the config.
Nina: Also add an e2e test that simulates 10K short requests + 200 concurrent long ones to ensure fairness invariants hold.
Sam: thanks team. If we see any regressions, revert kernel-score tweak first — it's the riskiest. :thumbsup:
Eli: noted. I'll keep an eye on canary traces and push additional telemetry if needed.
Maria: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/12345 — includes rollout plan and metrics dashboard link.
perf-bot: [alert muted] no high-severity regressions in first 2h.
Sam: closing loop later today after postmortem check.
Nina: will add a brief note to eng-runbook about the new short_reserve param and how to tune by tenant weight.
Eli: 👍
Maria: merging canary -> next stage in ~1h unless someone objects.
Sam: no objections. Thanks all.
